records.category: audit finding on misrecorded spending and misreported outputs
records.people: Rebeca Patricia Santos Rivera (President of the Banco Central de Honduras, addressee of the report); the bank's Unidad de Presupuesto and Organizacion y Planeamiento staff (not individually named)
records.summary: Honduras's supreme audit institution, the Tribunal Superior de Cuentas, evaluated the Banco Central de Honduras's accounting for its 2022 spending and concluded that expenditure had been booked under budget lines that do not match the state's budget-classification manual, that one publication was counted twice as a final output, and that the bank reported 100 per cent of its economic information as published while reports of the real sector had in fact been suspended since 2016. The report carries two binding recommendations to the bank's president.
records.quote: se registraron gastos que no corresponden a los conceptos establecidos en el manual de clasificadores presupuestarios
records.source_title: Informe RC-N°42-2023-DFEP-BCH, Evaluación a la Rendición de Cuentas de la Ejecución del Gasto practicada al Banco Central de Honduras, periodo fiscal 2022 (Tribunal Superior de Cuentas)

records.category: economic damage to the bank caused by its own staff
records.people: Richard Paolo Tejeda Pérez and María del Rosario Ramos Santos (former public servants of the Banco Central de Bolivia, the people paid); fifteen serving and former BCB public servants found to bear indications of joint civil liability (not named in the executive summary)
records.summary: An internal audit by the Gerencia de Auditoria Interna of the Banco Central de Bolivia, ordered by the bank's presidency and carried out under the norms of the Contraloria General del Estado, examined salaries and other benefits accrued and paid to two former BCB employees between 2021 and 2025 and concluded that there were indications of joint civil liability for economic damage to the bank of 104,787.54 bolivianos, against fifteen serving and former public servants, for acts and omissions in the exercise of their functions. Because the full sum was repaid to the bank's treasury on 23 July 2025 the audit office decided not to schedule a compliance audit.
records.source_title: Informe N° BCB-GAUD-INF-2025-58, Resumen Ejecutivo, Relevamiento de Información sobre salarios devengados y pagados a dos ex servidores públicos del BCB (Banco Central de Bolivia, Gerencia de Auditoría Interna, 6 November 2025)
records.notes: No quote field: the PDF's text layer garbles accented characters (it extracts 'daño' as 'daho'), so nothing could be copied character-for-character.

records.category: procurement breaches at the monetary authority
records.people: Cindy Scotland (Chief Executive Officer, Cayman Islands Monetary Authority); Garth MacDonald (Board Chairman); the Authority's own Entity Procurement Committee
records.summary: The Auditor General's general report on the Cayman Islands government's 2023 accounts set out four purchases by the Cayman Islands Monetary Authority made without the approval of the Authority's own Entity Procurement Committee as the Procurement Act requires: legal consultancy services of 163,000 dollars and three purchases of services valued at 103,000, 129,000 and 120,000 dollars. Questioned about them at a Public Accounts Committee hearing on 23 January 2025, the Authority's chief executive accepted responsibility and said procurement had since been centralised in one division.
records.quote: we didn't tick the boxes and do it the right way so for that, we take full responsibility
records.source_title: Report of the Standing Public Accounts Committee on the Auditor General's General Report 2023, Parliament of the Cayman Islands, January 2025 (verbatim hearing transcript, paragraph 58 of the Auditor General's report discussed)
records.notes: Person overlap flagged: Cindy Scotland also appears in the record the map already holds for CYM (index 203, the 2015 internal conflict-of-interest review). She was managing director throughout, so she appears in anything about this authority. The episode, the year, the conduct and the document are all different: a 2023 procurement finding by the Auditor General, discussed in Parliament in 2025, against a 2015 internal review of a staff conflict of interest.

records.category: corporate-governance audit finding: confidentiality declared without legal basis, no channel for reporting misconduct
records.people: Members of the Junta Directiva of the Banco Central de Costa Rica, its Gerencia and its Secretaría General (not individually named in the findings)
records.summary: The Contraloria General de la Republica (Costa Rica) rated the Banco Central de Costa Rica at partial compliance in a corporate-governance audit, report DFOE-FIP-IAD-00001-2024, published on 12 August 2024. Among the findings reported: of 53 physical board minutes containing at least one item declared confidential, 33 recorded no legal basis for the designation; board members failed to sign eight minutes from sessions between October 2022 and December 2023 on time, signature taking between one and fifteen months and sometimes being collected at members' homes; the bank had no rule or effective channel for reporting misconduct by directors and staff; and its corporate governance and ethics codes had not been updated in over ten years.
records.source_title: Contraloría reprueba prácticas del Banco Central, incluyendo declaratorias de confidencialidad y capacitación de directivos (El Observador, Costa Rica)
records.notes: This rests on a Costa Rican news outlet's report of the Contraloria's audit, not on report DFOE-FIP-IAD-00001-2024 itself, which was not opened. The report number and publication date are as the article gives them. No quote field: the article's Spanish was read through a fetch tool rather than copied from the page, so nothing could be guaranteed character-for-character. The same outlet is the source of the record the map already holds for CRI, but the episode is different: a 2024 governance audit of the bank, not the 2023 criminal complaint against the SUGEF superintendent.

records.category: contracting irregularities in the electronic money system
records.people: Banco Central del Ecuador staff responsible for the dinero electrónico contracts and records (not named); Diego Martínez (former head of the Banco Central del Ecuador) and Patricio Rivera (former Economy Minister), named by the source as the project's promoters rather than as subjects of the finding
records.summary: The Contraloria General del Estado examined more than 4.4 million dollars of contracts behind the Banco Central del Ecuador's dinero electronico system and delivered its results to the bank on 12 October 2018. It found that one contract was awarded to the Asociacion Inswitch-Adexus although the bidder did not meet the technical requirements in the terms of reference, leaving the bank's own staff without full administrative access to the system's database and dependent on the contractor to use an asset it had paid for; that contractors could still reach the system and potentially private information because it was never fully handed over; that some tools were contracted and never used; and that bank staff kept incomplete records of the system's acquisition and operation.
records.source_title: Hubo vacíos técnicos en el proyecto de dinero electrónico (Diario Expreso, Ecuador, 30 November 2018)
records.notes: This rests on an Ecuadorean newspaper's report of the Contraloria's examination, not on the Contraloria report itself, which the article does not number and which was not opened. No quote field, for the same reason as the Costa Rica record: the page was read through a fetch tool, not copied.

Five 2025 executive summaries were downloaded and read in full or grepped for deficienc/observaci/incumpl/responsabilidad/sanci: BCB-GAUD-INF-2025-21 (compliance of the bank's Comite de Control Interno with Contraloria resolutions CGE/112/2022 and CGE/114/2022 for 2024) concludes the committee complied and categorises the bank as RIESGO BAJO; BCB-GAUD-INF-2025-64 (definitive disposal of assets, gestion 2024, gratuitous transfer to sixteen La Paz schools) concludes the process complied with the NB-SABS and RE-SABS and that nothing warranted an audit or referral to the competent legal authority; 2025-33, 2025-43 and 2025-47 contain none of the finding vocabulary. The one that did, 2025-58, is filed as a record above. The remaining 2025 reports (13, 14, 27, 44, 46) and the 2020 and 2021 series were not opened and are the obvious next move for a third Bolivian record.

The Public Accounts Committee's report on the Auditor General's General Report 2023 was downloaded and read: the whole CIMA witness session (Cindy Scotland and Garth MacDonald, hearing of 23 January 2025) plus every mention of 'Monetary Authority', 'CIMA', 'procurement', 'breach' and 'non-compliance' in the 2,300-line transcript. Apart from the four procurements filed above, the only other matter against the Authority is its non-implementation of section 47(1) of the Public Authorities Act on pay parity, on which the Committee's sympathy was with CIMA; the transcript otherwise records an unqualified audit opinion and the Committee congratulating CIMA on its management and leadership. A statutory pay-parity gap is not misconduct and is not filed.
